papers.titleEn: Radical-Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO 2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Charge‐transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. Here, we report a radical‐mediated surface reconstruction strategy for ligand‐free SnO 2 nanocrystals that enables concurrent gains in device efficiency, scalability, and durability. Sonochemical activation generates hydroxyl radicals that selectively passivate oxygen‐deficient Sn sites while inducing electrostatically stabilized dispersions with exceptional shelf stability, allowing the SnO 2 colloids to be stored for over 2 years without aggregation or performance degradation. This stabilization enables the formation of uniform electron transport layers with reduced trap density and enhanced electron mobility. These improvements promote buried‐interface perovskite crystallization and accelerate charge extraction, yielding PSCs with an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 26.12%). Importantly, the strategy is inherently scalable, enabling a perovskite module (∼110 cm 2 ) with an efficiency of 21.45%. Devices exhibit enhanced operational stability, retaining 92% efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2), maintaining 88% efficiency under maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and showing negligible degradation over 500 thermal cycles (ISOS‐T‐3). These results establish radical‐mediated engineering of SnO 2 nanocrystals as a general pathway in perovskite photovoltaics, bridging high efficiency, large‐area manufacturability, and long‐term operational stability.
papers.filename: Liyuan Han, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2026, Radical-Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO 2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules

papers.titleEn: AI-Enabled Mixed Potential Sensor Array for Complex VOC Mixture Decoding and Real-Time Methanol-Risk Assessment in Baijiu
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of complex gas mixtures in dynamic real-world environments is essential for environmental monitoring, food safety, and public health. However, these challenges arise mainly from overlapping response fingerprints of chemically similar hazardous analytes and the limited capability of conventional sensors to decouple multicomponent, concentration-coupled signals. Here, we report a ZnFe2O4/MoO3 mixed potential sensor array enabled by a material-device-algorithm co-design strategy. Through compositional engineering of the sensing electrodes, the array generates orthogonal cross-reactive fingerprints for six volatile organic compounds, with response fluctuation standard deviations of 0.47-2.43 mV across all analytes and a rapid response time of 12 s toward 100 ppm triethylamine. To address alcohol mixtures with strong competitive adsorption, including methanol, ethanol, and n-butanol, a CNN-BiLSTM spatiotemporal fusion model extracts multiscale features from dynamic sensing responses, enabling simultaneous mixture classification and concentration prediction. The system achieves recognition accuracies of 100 and 99.33% for the test set and independent validation set, respectively, with corresponding mean absolute errors of 1.61 and 1.62 ppm. We further extend this strategy to a portable Baijiu MeOH sensing platform for real-time methanol-risk assessment in complex liquor matrices, achieving above 98.89% accuracy in identifying samples exceeding the statutory limit. This work integrates interfacial electrochemical regulation, high-dimensional array sensing, deep-learning-enabled signal decoupling, and portable system implementation, offering a deployable route toward intelligent gas sensing in complex real-world environments.
papers.filename: Tong Liu, ACS Sens., 2026, AI-Enabled Mixed Potential Sensor Array for Complex VOC Mixture Decoding and Real-Time Methanol-Risk Assessment in Baijiu

papers.titleEn: Transforming Cyclic Allenes into Precision Macromolecular Building Blocks
papers.abstract: Abstract Ring-opening allene metathesis polymerization (ROAlMP) provides direct access to polyallenamers containing reactive allene functionality within the polymer backbone, yet achieving controlled polymerization has remained a major challenge. Here, we report an additive-assisted ROAlMP strategy in which triphenylphosphine (PPh3) or 3,5-dichloropyridine (3,5-Cl2Py) modulates catalyst speciation to enable controlled polymerization behavior, affording polyallenamers with predictable molecular weight (Mn up to 70 kDa) and moderate dispersities (Đ < 1.4). This enhanced control enables the synthesis of di- and triblock copolymers spanning three distinct classes of metathesis-active monomers, including cyclic alkenes, diynes, and cyclic allenes, while also providing access to self-assembled nanostructured materials containing allene-rich domains. We further demonstrate that these domains can be selectively stabilized through backbone [2 + 2] photocrosslinking, a capability inherently encoded within the polymer backbone and achieved without additional monomer functionalization. Finally, to illustrate the unique chemical opportunities afforded by backbone allenes, the resulting polyallenamers were subjected to iodonium-induced annulation, generating naphthalene-containing polymer backbones with pronounced changes in their photophysical behavior. Collectively, these results establish additive-controlled ROAlMP as a versatile platform for precision polyallenamer synthesis and highlight the unique materials opportunities enabled by allene-containing polymer backbones.
papers.filename: William J. Neary, Macromolecules, 2026, Transforming Cyclic Allenes into Precision Macromolecular Building Blocks

papers.titleEn: Interleaving Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-selective contacts in inverted wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and non-uniform interfacial contact of the SAMs/absorber induce recombination losses and interfacial degradation. Herein, we introduce carbohydrazide (CBH) as an interfacial modifier by interleaving it with SAMs to remedy their uncovered and weakly contacted interfacial regions. The CBH treatment improves interfacial uniformity and strengthens hole extraction, primarily through its dipolar nature and favorable interactions with the perovskite surface. This enables a reduced interfacial defect density and substantially extended interfacial stability. As a result, the optimized WBG perovskite single-junction device achieves a top power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.51% (19.56% for control), accompanied by a high open-circuit voltage of 1.355 V. Extending this approach to tandem architectures, its two-terminal all-perovskite tandem solar cell and monolithic mini-module reach impressive PCEs of 29.35% and 23.41% (20.07 cm2), respectively. Both single-junction and tandem devices exhibit pronouncedly improved operational stability. This work provides an innovative and effective strategy to address SAM-related buried interfacial challenges for inverted WBG PSCs.
papers.filename: Jiang Tang, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Interleaving Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules

papers.titleEn: Etching-Assisted Double-End Anchoring of Ligands for High-Performance CsPbBr3 Light-Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as highly promising emitters for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) owing to their outstanding luminescence properties, broadly tunable band structures, and intrinsically high color purity. Surface ligand engineering plays a crucial role in regulating the electroluminescent performance and device stability of perovskite NCs. Here, we develop a cooperative 2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)phenyl)ethylamine (MSPE)-hydrogen halide (HX, X = Br, I) ligand-exchange strategy that enables surface reconfiguration and robust passivation of perovskite NCs. In this approach, HX assists in removing insulating long-chain ligands (oleic acid and oleylamine), thereby exposing additional undercoordinated surface sites and promoting firm double-end anchoring of in situ protonated MSPE through bidentate interactions. Spectroscopic and electrical analyses reveal that the strengthened ligand-nanocrystal interface effectively suppresses trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, increases the exciton binding energy from 97.7 to 168.9 meV, prolongs the lifetime from 9.5 to 12.3 ns, and reduces trap densities in CsPbBr3 NC films. As a result, the photoluminescence quantum yield of CsPbBr3 NCs after MSPE-HBr treatment is enhanced to 96.1%, and LEDs fabricated with MSPE-HBr-treated NCs deliver a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.2% and display excellent device-to-device reproducibility. This cooperative ligand-exchange strategy provides an effective pathway for achieving high surface coverage of robust multidentate ligands, offering a promising route toward highly efficient and stable perovskite LEDs.
papers.filename: Ying Ma, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Etching-Assisted Double-End Anchoring of Ligands for High-Performance CsPbBr3 Light-Emitting Diodes
